points.description: States that there are four ways to pass a pointer to a function, and that these combine pointer constness (nonconstant/constant pointer) with data constness (constant/nonconstant data).
Names nonconstant pointer to constant data AND nonconstant pointer to nonconstant data precisely, with the terms 'constant' and 'nonconstant' applied correctly to pointer and data.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only one of the two is named precisely

points.description: Names constant pointer to constant data AND constant pointer to nonconstant data precisely, with the terms 'constant' and 'nonconstant' applied correctly to pointer and data.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only one of the two is named precisely

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four combinations named with correct pointer/data constness terminology, and the count of four. Part marks only where one of the two items in a point is precise. A vague answer (e.g. 'by value, by reference'), a swapped or wrong combination, or a wrong extra item earns nothing for the affected point.
